# P2.4 text-editing fixtures (the §6 gate matrix)

These PDFs are the **gate** for P2.4 Stage 1 (constrained in-place text editing). They
are deliberately tiny, committed, and generated by `src-tauri/src/editor/testpdf.rs`
through lopdf's **public API only** — the same library the product writes with — so a
fixture that lopdf cannot express is a real signal about what Stage 1 can express.

Regenerate with:

```bash
scripts/make-p24-fixtures.sh
```

Only re-run when a builder in `testpdf.rs` changes; the committed bytes are what the
tests read.

## Which gate each fixture exercises

| Fixture | Gate (P2.4 §3) | What it must provoke |
|---------|----------------|----------------------|
| `simple-winansi.pdf` | happy path | `/Type1 /Helvetica /WinAnsiEncoding`, three pages, two runs each. Editable. |
| `simple-embedded-subset.pdf` | (c) not subset | `ABCDEF+` prefix on `/BaseFont` → `TEXT_RUN_NOT_EDITABLE`, gate `not-subset`. |
| `cid-identity.pdf` | (a) simple font | `/Type0` + `/Identity-H` → `TEXT_RUN_NOT_EDITABLE`, gate `simple-font`. |
| `roundtrip-fail.pdf` | (b) encoding round-trip | `/Differences` with two names mapping to U+0020, so a byte decodes to a space and re-encodes to a *different* byte → gate `encoding-round-trip`. |
| `too-wide.pdf` | (d) width | One very short run (`HI`), so a plausible replacement overflows the advance width → `TEXT_RUN_NOT_EDITABLE`, gate `fits-width`, quoting both measured widths. The gate is evaluated at edit time from PDFium-measured widths; the fixture only has to provide a genuinely narrow run. |
| `encrypted-aes.pdf` | T7 / T8 | AES-128, user password `secret`. Opens read-only; every edit refuses `ENCRYPTED_READ_ONLY`; "Decrypt a copy" produces `{stem} (unprotected).pdf`. |
| `multi-stream-page.pdf` | F2 collapse | `/Contents` is an array of two streams. lopdf concatenates them, so runs from both are located and the edited page collapses to one stream (legal; D2 copy semantics leave the original's layout alone). |
| `reflow-line.pdf` | P2.8 §6.2, row A10 | Line 1 is one `TJ` array — `ALPHA `, a `-120` kern, `BETA` — behind a **single** `Td`, so moving its tail must *insert* a positioning operator; line 2 (`WXYZ`) is placed by its own `Tm` and must not move. Ends 389 pt clear of the 612 pt box. |
| `reflow-line-near-edge.pdf` | P2.8 §6.2, R3 refusal | The same two lines starting at x=452, so line 1 ends **9.064 pt** from the box — less than one replacement's worth of room, which is what `fits-width` needs in order to refuse. |
| `bomb.pdf` | (e) / F3 cap | A 16 MiB stream that compresses to a few KB, beyond the 8 MiB `CONTENT_LIMIT` → `CONTENT_TOO_LARGE`. |

## Honest limitations

Two gates cannot be produced as a *committed file* that also behaves as the gate
requires, because a PDF that genuinely exhibits the failure would need a font program
this repo does not ship. Both are covered by in-memory unit tests in
`src/editor/textedit.rs` and `src/editor/testlocate.rs`, which build the same shape with
lopdf and assert the refusal — so **no gate is untested**:

* **Gate (b), round-trip failure.** The committed `roundtrip-fail.pdf` carries the
  `/Differences` collision, and lopdf's own `get_font_encoding`/`string_to_bytes` decides
  the verdict at runtime. That is the honest, non-hand-crafted version of the fixture:
  the gate fires because lopdf's inverse map really does lose one of the two names. The
  unit test `refuses_an_unroundtrippable_encoding_with_gate_b` asserts it directly.
* **Gate (c), subset font.** The `ABCDEF+` prefix is real subset-naming evidence and is
  all the gate inspects (Stage 1 does not open the embedded program — T11). The committed
  fixture therefore *does* provoke the refusal; the note here is only that it is a name
  convention we match rather than a program we parse.

`sample.pdf` predates this matrix and remains the best-case regression fixture for the
earlier phases.

## Forms fixtures (P3.3)

Unlike the P2.4 matrix above, these are **not** built by `testpdf.rs`. They are produced by
real third-party writers, because the point of the fixture is a spelling this repository would
not have chosen to write.

| Fixture | Producer | What it must provoke |
|---------|----------|----------------------|
| `libreoffice-checkbox-form.pdf` | LibreOffice 24.2.7.2, `--convert-to 'pdf:writer_pdf_Export:{"ExportFormFields":{"type":"boolean","value":"true"}}'` on an HTML form | A checkbox whose **on state is `/Yes` while its single appearance stream is keyed `/yes`**. Also `/NeedAppearances true`. |

### Why the LibreOffice checkbox fixture exists

**This fixture is the reason the writer accepts the lower-case `/yes` state.**

LibreOffice writes the widget's value as the **name `/Yes`** and its default as `/DV /Yes`,
but names the *appearance* stream **`/yes`** — lower case:

```
/V /Yes          /DV /Yes          /N << /yes 26 0 R /Off 27 0 R >>          /AS /Yes
```

ISO 32000-1 requires `/AS` to name a key present in `/AP /N`, and here it does not, by case.
A writer that assumes the state name is spelled one way — `/Yes`, or `/On`, or upper case
generally — picks the wrong key, or writes `/AS` naming a stream that no viewer can find, and
the box renders unticked while the value reads back correct. The design ruling (P3.3 D-F3) is
therefore that `/V` and `/AS` are taken as **names from the field's own `/AP /N` keys**, never
from a hardcoded spelling. This file is the evidence for that decision, so it stays in the tree
rather than being regenerated into a tidier shape.

The three spellings the writer must survive are `/On`, `/Yes`, and `/yes`. The control fixture
for `/Yes`/`/Off` is produced by `reportlab`; this one supplies the odd case.

**Personal data:** none. The fields are `fullname` (empty) and `agree`. No `/Author`, `/Title`
or `/Subject` is set; the only metadata is `/Producer LibreOffice 24.2` and a creation date,
which is the producer identity this README relies on.

### The synthesised matrix (`form-*.pdf`)

`libreoffice-checkbox-form.pdf` above is the only real producer this repo commits, and it happens to
spell its appearance key `/yes`. That is a *sample* of the wild, not the wild: a writer that
hardcodes `/yes` passes it. The matrix below is built by `testpdf` so the spellings that no producer
here emits can be written on purpose.

| Fixture | What it must provoke |
|---------|----------------------|
| `form-text-fields.pdf` | `/Tx`, one single-line (`given`) and one multi-line (`notes`, `/Ff` bit 13). The type PDFium already fills correctly, so it is the control for every writer assertion. |
| `form-checkbox-yes.pdf` | `/Btn` with on-state `/Yes` — the reportlab spelling. |
| `form-checkbox-on.pdf` | `/Btn` with on-state `/On`. No producer here emits this, so a writer that hardcodes `/Yes` fails here and nowhere else. W4's primary pixel case. |
| `form-checkbox-lowercase-yes.pdf` | `/Btn` with on-state `/yes`. Isolates the lower-case key from the LibreOffice file's separate `/V`/`/AS` disagreement. |
| `form-radio-group.pdf` | Parent `/FT /Btn` with `/Ff` bit 16 and two kids naming `/red` and `/blue`. A writer reading only the parent finds no state to write. |
| `form-choice-fields.pdf` | `/Ch`: a combo (`pick`, `/Ff` bit 18, no `/V`) and a multi-select list (`many`, bit 22, with `/I` and a matching `/V`). |
| `form-read-only.pdf` | `/Tx` with `/Ff` bit 1. W6's I-F4 refusal. |
| `form-xfa.pdf` | An `/XFA` entry in the catalog's `/AcroForm`, which this build refuses by name (D-F6). |

Every appearance stream draws different ink on and off, because W4 compares rendered pixels of the
widget rectangle: a fixture whose on-state drew the same box as its off-state would let any writer
pass. `scripts/make-p33-fixtures.sh` is the generator, and the generator asserts that two builds of
each document are byte-identical before writing anything, so a pixel gate cannot fail for a reason
that has nothing to do with the code under test.

### pdfium-render cannot enumerate `/AP` state names

Measured, and it changes the design. `pdfium-render 0.8.37` exposes a field's `/AS` (as
`appearance_stream()`) and its `/V`, but the only `/AP` accessor is `FPDFAnnot_GetAP`, which returns
the *selected* stream — not the key set under `/AP /N`. So a button's on/off names cannot be read
through PDFium at all.

D-F3 says "state names come from `/AP`". That is still the rule; what changes is *who reads it*: the
names are read from the same lopdf document the writer mutates, not from the PDFium field. Reading
them from lopdf is also stricter — it is the exact dictionary the write lands in, so a name cannot
differ between the read and the write.

**Regenerate** (output is not byte-identical — LibreOffice stamps a creation date and object
numbers vary, so regenerate only to replace the file deliberately, and re-check the `/N` keys
afterwards):

```bash
cat > /tmp/form.html <<'HTML'
<html><body><h1>Fixture</h1><form>
<p>Name: <input type="text" name="fullname" value=""></p>
<p>Agree: <input type="checkbox" name="agree" value="yes" checked></p>
</form></body></html>
HTML
soffice --headless \
  --convert-to 'pdf:writer_pdf_Export:{"ExportFormFields":{"type":"boolean","value":"true"}}' \
  --outdir /tmp /tmp/form.html
```
